overview: Consolidated Edison, Inc. is a regulated utility holding company whose principal subsidiary, Consolidated Edison Company of New York (CECONY), delivers electricity, natural gas, and steam to roughly 3.6 million customers in New York City and Westchester County. Orange and Rockland Utilities (O&R) provides regulated electric and gas service in adjacent parts of New York and New Jersey, while Con Edison Transmission develops and holds joint-venture interests in electric and gas transmission assets. Since exiting its unregulated Clean Energy Businesses (sold to RWE in 2023), Con Edison is now an almost purely rate-regulated, capital-intensive utility whose earnings growth is driven by rate-base expansion tied to grid modernization, resiliency, and electrification investment in one of the densest and highest-cost-of-service territories in the U.S.

business_model.summary: Con Edison earns a regulated return on invested capital (rate base) set by the New York Public Service Commission (NYPSC) and New Jersey regulators for O&R. Revenue is generated by delivering electricity, natural gas, and steam under cost-of-service rate plans, with earnings growth driven almost entirely by capital investment in grid infrastructure (rate base growth), authorized ROE, and reconciliation/true-up mechanisms rather than volumetric demand growth.
business_model.customer_type: Regulated B2C and B2B; ~3.6 million electric and gas customers in NYC/Westchester, plus O&R territory; heavy commercial/real-estate and institutional load concentration in Manhattan
business_model.geographic_mix: Almost entirely New York State (NYC and Westchester County via CECONY; Rockland/Orange counties and parts of NJ via O&R); no material international or unregulated exposure post Clean Energy Businesses sale

competitive_position.market_position: Monopoly regulated utility with an exclusive electric, gas, and steam distribution franchise in New York City and Westchester County; not directly competitive with peer utilities operationally (non-overlapping service territories) but compared for capital allocation, valuation, and regulatory benchmarking purposes

moat_factors.description: Exclusive right to deliver electricity, gas, and steam in NYC/Westchester; no realistic competitor can duplicate the wires/pipes network
Enormous capital cost and permitting complexity of building competing distribution infrastructure in dense urban NYC market
Only investor-owned utility in the U.S. operating a district steam system at this scale (Manhattan), a legacy asset with limited but sticky commercial/institutional demand
Long operating history with NYPSC provides some predictability, though recent rate cases have been contentious

weaknesses: Rate case friction: NYPSC and elected officials pushed back hard on 2026 rate filings, approving only a fraction of ConEd's original ask, showing political sensitivity around NYC energy affordability
No growth optionality outside regulated NY/NJ footprint since Clean Energy Businesses divestiture — pure regulated-utility growth ceiling
Aging, dense urban infrastructure (Manhattan underground network) is expensive to maintain and upgrade versus greenfield utility footprints
Steam business is in secular decline as buildings electrify, a stranded-asset risk over the long term
High customer bills relative to national average make ConEd a frequent political target for rate scrutiny

growth_drivers: Multi-year, multi-billion-dollar capital investment plan (~$38B company-wide, ~$27B+ at CECONY through 2030) driving regulated rate-base growth of roughly 8%+ annually
Grid modernization and resiliency spending (substations, storm hardening, undergrounding) required by state climate law and reliability mandates
Building and transportation electrification (EV charging, electric heat pumps) increasing new electric business load — ~44% of new business load requests tied to electrification
Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) rollout (~$1.55B of 2026-2030 capex)
Con Edison Transmission joint-venture growth in interstate/interregional transmission projects supporting New York's clean energy transition (CLCPA compliance)
Constructive multi-year rate plans (2026-2028 approved increases) providing revenue visibility and reduced regulatory lag
52-consecutive-year dividend growth track record (Dividend Aristocrat/King) supporting income-oriented investor demand
Potential incremental data center/large-load demand at the margin, though NYC territory sees less data-center buildout than upstate NY or other regions

business.description: 2026 NY rate case saw ConEd's original electric revenue request cut by ~87%; heightened political and consumer scrutiny over NYC energy affordability could compress future authorized returns
Building electrification and NYC's Climate Mobilization Act reduce long-term demand for steam heating, risking stranded assets
Manhattan's dense underground electric/gas network requires continuous, costly maintenance and carries outage/incident risk

business.risk: Execution risk on large capex plan
business.description: Delivering ~$7B+/year of capital projects on budget and on schedule across substations, AMI, and transmission JV projects

financial.risk: High leverage / heavy equity issuance needs
financial.description: Plans to issue ~$1.85B of common equity in 2026 and up to $4.3B 2027-2029 to fund capex, creating dilution risk and reliance on capital markets access

As a capital-intensive, debt-funded utility, financing costs and valuation are highly sensitive to interest rate levels; higher-for-longer rates pressure cost of capital and bond-proxy valuation multiples
Gap between capital spend and rate recovery can compress near-term earnings and cash flow

regulatory.risk: New York Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act (CLCPA) compliance costs
regulatory.description: Mandated shift away from fossil-fuel gas/steam infrastructure requires substantial capital reallocation and creates stranded-asset risk for gas system

regulatory.risk: NYC Climate Mobilization Act (Local Law 97) building emissions rules
regulatory.description: Accelerates building electrification, pressuring gas/steam volumes while requiring new electric infrastructure investment

regulatory.risk: Non-executive incentive compensation audit and other NYPSC compliance reviews
regulatory.description: Statewide audit and ongoing regulatory compliance burdens could result in disallowed costs or penalties
Authorized ROE and revenue requirements are subject to renegotiation at each rate case; political pressure could compress future ROE relative to peers

macro.description: Utility valuations trade as bond proxies; rate volatility affects both cost of debt/equity financing and stock multiple
Severe storms, flooding, and heat events in the NYC metro area drive restoration costs and resiliency capex, with recovery subject to regulatory approval
Gas costs are largely passed through to customers, limiting direct margin risk, but volatility affects customer affordability and political pressure on rates

execution.description: $38B+ multi-year capex plan requires sustained permitting, contractor capacity, and cost discipline across substations, AMI, and transmission JV projects
Balancing multi-billion-dollar equity issuance with EPS growth targets requires careful capital markets execution

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. regulated utility sector benefiting from a multi-year capex supercycle driven by grid modernization, electrification, and (in many territories) data center/AI load growth; New York-specific growth is more electrification- and resiliency-driven than data-center-driven relative to peers in Virginia, Texas, or the Southeast
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - regulated utility with highly predictable, non-discretionary demand (electricity, gas, steam essential services); earnings driven by rate base and regulatory outcomes rather than economic cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - capital-intensive business reliant on debt and equity issuance to fund capex; stock trades partly as a bond proxy and multiple compresses when rates rise
key_input_costs: Equipment and materials (transformers, cable, substations) amid supply chain and tariff-related cost inflation

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 earnings: net income for common stock rose to $308M ($0.83/share) from $246M ($0.68/share) in Q2 2025; revenues of $4.07B up 13.2% YoY, beating consensus; company reaffirmed FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance of $6.00-$6.20

NYPSC approved a scaled-back multi-year rate plan after major public/political pushback on ConEd's original request; approved electric increases of 3.5% (2026), 3.2% (2027), 3.1% (2028) and gas increases of 4.4% (2026), 5.7% (2027), 5.6% (2028), cutting the original electric revenue request by roughly 87% in year one

Company unveiled/reaffirmed an approximately $38 billion five-year (2026-2030) capital investment plan, including ~$27B+ at CECONY, with plans to place 28 new substations in service by 2035 and ~$29B directed at grid modernization for rising electrification

Completed final wind-down items related to the 2023 Clean Energy Businesses sale to RWE, including the transfer of the Broken Bow II wind project for ~$54 million, closing out the company's exit from unregulated renewables
Company continued to extend its dividend growth streak to 52 consecutive years, reinforcing its Dividend Aristocrat/Dividend King status
Morgan Stanley cut its price target on ED from $101 to $97 while maintaining an Underweight rating, reflecting a cautious sell-side view even as the stock has performed well year-to-date

items.notes: Growth rate applied off the midpoint of 2026 adjusted EPS guidance as the base year
Includes ~$7.3B in 2026 ramping to ~$9.1B by 2030; ~$29B directed at grid modernization/electrification; 28 new substations by 2035
Primary driver of regulated earnings growth

items.target: ~$1,850 million in 2026; up to $4,300 million aggregate 2027-2029
items.notes: Funds the multi-year capital plan; creates modest annual EPS dilution offset by rate-base earnings growth

guidance.management_commentary: Management reaffirmed 2026 adjusted EPS guidance and the 6-7% long-term EPS growth algorithm following Q2 2026 results, emphasizing continued rate-base growth from grid modernization, resiliency, and electrification investment, alongside the newly approved multi-year rate plans that provide several years of revenue and cost-recovery visibility. Management has also highlighted managing customer affordability concerns following political pushback on the 2026 rate case as an ongoing area of focus.

bull_case: Highly predictable, regulated earnings stream with multi-year rate plans (through 2028) now in place, reducing regulatory lag risk
52 consecutive years of dividend growth (Dividend King) appeals to income-oriented investors seeking a durable, defensive yield
Large, visible capital investment runway (~$38B through 2030) supports high-single-digit rate base growth and a 6-7% long-term EPS growth algorithm
Monopoly franchise in one of the wealthiest, densest service territories in the U.S. (NYC/Westchester) provides a durable, irreplaceable asset base
Electrification of buildings and transportation in New York provides a structural, multi-decade tailwind to electric delivery volumes and capex needs
bear_case: 2026 rate case outcome (regulators cut the original ask by ~87% in year one) signals rising political risk to future authorized returns and cost recovery in a high-profile, affordability-sensitive market
High interest-rate sensitivity as a heavily debt- and equity-funded capital spender; a higher-for-longer rate environment raises financing costs and compresses the bond-proxy valuation multiple
Consensus analyst rating is Hold/Neutral with several Sell ratings and price targets clustered near or below the current share price, implying limited near-term upside per Wall Street
Steam business faces secular decline from electrification and NYC's Local Law 97, a slow-moving stranded-asset risk within the regulated portfolio
Continued heavy equity issuance (up to ~$6B+ cumulative 2026-2029) creates ongoing dilution that management must outrun with rate-base earnings growth to deliver per-share value
